site.home_lead: Make a prediction, investigate the phenomenon with a simulation or data, and build the explanation yourself.
site.home_description: Upper secondary physics through investigation: predictions, simulations, explanations and exercises, LOPS 2019 modules FY1–FY8.
site.home_path_herata: a phenomenon and the question the chapter answers
site.home_path_ennusta: commit to your own prediction before the results
site.home_path_tutki: experiment with a simulation or data and record what you see
site.home_path_selita: the explanation and the formula are built from the observations

home_start_items: Start from the first chapter of a module, or from the chapter your class is working on.
Predict first: once you have committed to an answer, you notice what is surprising in the investigation.
Use the simulation like an experiment: change one thing at a time and record what happens.
Open an answer or a model solution only after you have tried yourself, and compare yours with it step by step.
Do the core exercises; the others are extra practice, and level 3 is challenging application.
At the end of a chapter, go on to Next chapter.

module_question.FY1: How does physics measure and explain the world, from protons to galaxies?
module_question.FY2: Where does our energy come from, and how does using it affect the environment?
module_question.FY3: How is energy transferred as heat and work, and how does it change matter?
module_question.FY4: How do forces change the motion of an object?
module_question.FY5: Why do objects rotate and oscillate, and how do waves travel?
module_question.FY6: How does electric current flow in a circuit and transfer energy?
module_question.FY7: How are electricity and magnetism linked, and what is light?
module_question.FY8: Why is the energy of an atom quantised, and where does radiation come from?

lesson.exercise_path: You do not need to do every exercise. Start with the core exercises: they practise the main points of the chapter. The other exercises of levels 1 and 2 are extra practice if you want more certainty, and level 3 is challenging application.
lesson.level_lead_1: One formula or one step of reasoning. Core exercises first, the rest is extra practice.
lesson.level_lead_2: Two steps, a unit conversion or rearranging a formula. Core exercises first, the rest is extra practice.
lesson.level_lead_3: Optional: application, two ideas together or a new situation where you reason for yourself.
lesson.check_howto: Type your answer and press Check. The answer is checked in your browser and nothing is saved.
lesson.exercises_pending: The exercises for this lesson are still being checked. They will appear here when the check is done.
lesson.notice_legacy: Prototype version: this lesson was published before the current review process and is waiting to be renewed. The content may still change.
lesson.notice_draft: Draft: this lesson has not been reviewed yet.

practice.title: Apply independently
practice.eyebrow: {{code}} · at the end of the module
practice.description: {{code}} {{title}}: exercises to solve independently, model answers and marking guides for self-assessment.
practice.lead: In these tasks nobody tells you which formula to use. Decide yourself which phenomena and models belong to the situation, solve the task on paper and justify your solution, as in the matriculation examination.
practice.howto: Solve the task yourself first, on paper or on a computer. You may use a calculator, a data booklet and graphing software. Write out your reasoning, formulas, substitutions and answers with units.
practice.reveal: Show the model answer and marking
practice.reveal_hint: Open only when your own solution is ready.
practice.rubric_lead: Compare your solution with the model answer and, for each item, choose the points you think your solution earns. Part marks are possible, and any other physically correct method is accepted too.
practice.own_rubric_lead: For each item, choose the points you think your report earns.
practice.rubric_note: The points are your own estimate, not a checked grade. The marking is Ruukkilabra's own, written according to the features of a good matriculation examination answer, and it is not official marking by the Matriculation Examination Board (YTL).
practice.course_lead: At the end of the module you can try whether you can apply what you have learned independently, in the style of the matriculation examination. The model answers and marking guides open after your own solution.

criteria.graph_axes: The axes show the correct quantities and units, and the scales are evenly spaced.
criteria.graph_points: Each measurement is marked as a separate point in the right place.
criteria.graph_fit: The model is fitted to the points it suits, and the points have not been joined into a broken line.
criteria.graph_read: The slope or other quantity is read visibly from the graph, using two points on the line that are far apart.
criteria.equation: The starting equation is correct, and the quantity asked for is solved from it before the numbers are substituted.
criteria.calculation: The numerical values are substituted with their units, and the calculation is correct.
criteria.units_precision: The answer has the correct unit and a precision that matches the given data.
criteria.reasonableness: The reasonableness of the result has been assessed.
criteria.uncertainty: The uncertainty of the measurement has been estimated.
criteria.error_sources: The main sources of error are named, and it is explained how they affect the result.
criteria.assumptions: The assumption is named, and its effect on the result is justified.
criteria.conclusion: The conclusion answers the question and is based on the data.
criteria.fbd_object: The object is clearly chosen, and only the forces acting on it are drawn.
criteria.fbd_forces: Every force acting on the object is included, and there are no invented forces.
criteria.fbd_directions: Every force points in the physically correct direction.
criteria.fbd_representation: Each force arrow starts at a sensible point on the object, and each force has its own unambiguous name.
criteria.fbd_magnitudes: The arrow lengths are in the right proportion where the sizes are known, and forces are not mixed up with components, velocity or acceleration.
criteria.fbd_equations: The equations of motion come from the free-body diagram: the axes and the positive direction are chosen, and the signs are right.
